extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary) and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining patents and asserted claims in ex parte reexamination proceedings, including claim construction, statutory limits, prior-art treatment, amendments, and ancillary procedural matters. Focuses on how examiners should evaluate reexam requests and examine amended/new claims under relevant statutes and precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of judicial claim interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is related litigation and a federal court has made a judicial interpretation of a disputed claim term, the examiner in treating the disputed claim term should set forth his or her reasoning by, for example, acknowledging the judicial interpretation and assessing whether the judicial interpretation is consistent with the broadest reasonable construction of the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adopting a different claim construction than the judicial interpretation, the examiner should supply reasoning to support the different interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of patent owner statements (35 U.S.C.301(a)(2) / 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C.301(a)(2) permits submission of written statements of the patent owner filed in a proceeding before a federal court or the Office in which the patent owner took a position on the scope of any claim of a particular patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552, any such written statement of the patent owner of record in the patent (including reexamination files) should be considered (after reexamination ordered, but not at the order stage) to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim when applying patents or printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard in reexamination (35 U.S.C.304 and 257)
rubrics_metrics.description: During reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, and also under 35 U.S.C. 257, claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification and limitations in the specification are not read into the claims (In re Yamamoto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reexamination involving claims of an expired patent, apply Phillips ordinary-and-customary-meaning construction (words given their ordinary and customary meaning as understood by a person of ordinary skill at the time of the invention). The statutory presumption of validity (35 U.S.C. 282) has no application in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on 35 U.S.C.112 issues in reexamination under 304
rubrics_metrics.description: In reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, consideration of 35 U.S.C. 112 issues should be limited to the amendatory (e.g., new language) matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim amended or newly presented containing a limitation not found in the original patent claim should be considered for compliance under 35 U.S.C.112 only with respect to that limitation. Terms/limitations present in the original patent claim generally should not be reexamined under 112 in a 304 proceeding unless the amendatory matter creates the issue (e.g., rewriting a dependent claim as independent that creates lack of antecedent). However, priority/benefit date determinations under 112 are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of enablement/description and definiteness for new/amended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance of new or amended claims with the enablement and/or description requirements of the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C.112 and with the second paragraph of 35 U.S.C.112 should be considered as to the amendatory and new text in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2163 - § 2173.05(v) for extensive guidance on these matters; limit examination to the new/amended matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new matter (35 U.S.C.132/305) in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C.305 provides for examination under 35 U.S.C.132, which prohibits the introduction of new matter into the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where new matter is added to the claims or affects claim limitations, the claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C.112, first paragraph, for failing to meet the written description requirement. See MPEP § 2163.06 regarding the relationship between written description and the new matter prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of amendment to the specification on 35 U.S.C.112 compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to the specification can redefine the scope of the terms in a claim such that the claim is no longer clear or is not supported by the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should ensure that requirements of 35 U.S.C.112 are met when the specification is amended because such amendments can cause claims to fail compliance even if claims themselves are not amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must not enlarge scope of patent (35 U.S.C.305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new or amended claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, the claims of the reexamination proceeding should be examined under 35 U.S.C.305 to determine whether they enlarge the scope of the original claims. 35 U.S.C.305 states that 'no proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of the claims of the patent will be permitted in a reexamination proceeding....'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim 'enlarges the scope' where it is broader than each and every claim of the patent. A claim is broadened if it contains any conceivable product/process that would not have infringed the original patent or if it is broader in any one respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and explanation of broadening claim limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a rejection under 35 U.S.C.305, the claim limitations considered to broaden the scope should be identified and explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.11 for rejections under 35 U.S.C.305; bracketed portions should identify the claim and explain why/which limitations broaden scope. Examiner Note: identify the claim limitations in bracket 2 and explain per MPEP § 2258.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling patents with prior Office or court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some claims in a patent being reexamined have been the subject of a prior Office or court decision, those claims should be identified and handled per MPEP § 2242; copending proceedings addressed in MPEP §§2282-2286.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent claims not subject to reexamination because of prior adjudication should be identified. For claims dependent on a claim not subject to reexamination, see MPEP § 2260.01. If grounds in a prior Office/court decision are not based on patents/printed publications and clearly raise validity questions, the examiner’s Office action should state that the claims have not been examined as to those non-patent/non-printed-publication grounds (37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to 'live' claims for which reexamination was requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office’s determination will generally be limited solely to review of the 'live' claims (existing claims not held invalid by a final decision) for which reexamination has been requested. If requester did not request reexamination of certain claims, those claims generally will not be reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C.302 requires the request must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested (37 CFR 1.510(b)). If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims. The Office, however, has discretion to reexamine non-requested claims under 35 U.S.C.303(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office discretion to add or reexamine non-requested claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to reexamine any claim for which reexamination has not been requested lies within the sole discretion of the Office and may be exercised based on individual facts of each case. The Office may also initiate reexamination on its own initiative (35 U.S.C.303(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art is discovered during reexamination that raises a substantial new question of patentability as to claims not ordered for reexamination under 35 U.S.C.304, such claims may be added during the examination phase at the Office’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice is improper in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding since no statutory basis exists for restriction in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of claims to a 'separate and distinct' invention to the patent would be considered an enlargement of scope. See Ex parte Wikdahl and MPEP § 1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary matters permissible in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: There are matters ancillary to reexamination that are necessary and incident to patentability which will be considered, e.g., amendments to correct inadvertent failures to claim foreign priority or continuing status if necessary to overcome a reference applied against a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments may be made where necessary to address patentability issues discovered during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination (37 CFR 1.324)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be made during reexamination per 37 CFR 1.324 and MPEP § 1481 for petitions for correction of inventorship in a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.324 is granted, a Certificate of Correction indicating the change of inventorship will not be separately issued because the information is merged into the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits in reexamination (37 CFR 1.131, 1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131(a) and 1.132 may be utilized in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131(a) may not be used to 'swear behind' a reference patent if the reference patent is claiming the 'same invention' as the patent undergoing reexamination. The patent owner may, if appropriate, raise such issues via 1.131(c) or in an interference/derivation or reissue as applicable (see MPEP §§718, 1449.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not considered in reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C.304
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions other than those indicated for 304 (e.g., patentability based on public use or on sale, conduct issues, abandonment under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C.102(c), etc.) that are raised by the requester or patent owner will be noted by the examiner in an Office action but should not be independently raised by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.03 to indicate issues not within the scope of ex parte reexamination. If such questions are independently discovered by the examiner but were not raised by the requester or patent owner, they will not be noted in an Office action because 37 CFR 1.552(c) is limited to questions raised by the patent owner or requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preissuance submissions in reexamination (35 U.S.C.122(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Because reexamination is a post-issuance proceeding, a preissuance submission under 35 U.S.C.122(e) is not permitted to be filed in a reexamination proceeding; 35 U.S.C.122(e) is limited to preissuance submissions by third parties in patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preissuance submission filed in a reexamination proceeding is not to be entered and will be expunged if inadvertently entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for previously cited/considered art ('old art') before making rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: At the examining stage of a reexamination proceeding, the examiner will consider whether claims are subject to rejection based on art and should check the patent’s file history to ascertain whether the art that will provide the basis for the rejection was previously cited/considered in an earlier concluded Office examination (termed 'old art').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection will be based on a combination of old art and art newly cited during reexamination, the rejection is proper (In re Hiniker). Special rules apply when old art is the sole basis depending on the order date of reexamination (see following criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using old art as sole basis for SNQ — reexamination ordered on/after Nov 2, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered on or after November 2, 2002, reliance solely on old art does not necessarily preclude the existence of a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) based exclusively on that old art; determinations are fact-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A SNQ may be based solely on old art where the old art is being presented/viewed in a new light or different way compared with earlier examinations, in view of a material new argument or interpretation presented in the request. When an Office action first sets forth an SNQ based solely on old art (not in the order), include form paragraph 22.01.01 and explain how the old art is being applied and why it raises an SNQ. This form paragraph is used only the first time the old art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using old art as sole basis for SNQ — reexamination ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002 (Portola Packaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered prior to November 2, 2002, old art generally cannot be used as the sole basis for a rejection; presence/absence of SNQ is controlled by In re Portola Packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines: ascertain order date, determine what prior art in prior related Office proceedings was relied upon to reject or was cited and discussed, and base rejections at least in part on art that was neither relied upon nor discussed previously. Withdraw rejections based only on art previously relied upon/discussed. Terminate prosecution if only remaining rejections are entirely based on such prior art. The Director may search for new art before terminating. Follow detailed procedures in the MPEP for ongoing reexaminations ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for unusual fact patterns regarding old art
rubrics_metrics.description: Each case must be decided on its particular facts; unusual fact patterns (e.g., prior art was relied on or discussed previously but new evidence shows prior examiner did not appreciate relevant issues) should be brought to the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) or Technology Center (TC) Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of other evidence: nature of prior art, prosecution history, or admissions by patent owner/applicant/inventor. See 37 CFR 1.104(c)(3) for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language prior art previously cited — new translation may support reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign language prior art reference was cited and discussed in any prior Office proceeding but was never completely and accurately translated into English during the original prosecution, a more complete and accurate translation may justify reexamination based on that reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reexamination request should explain why the more complete and accurate translation actually teaches what is required by the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of cumulative (repetitive) references
rubrics_metrics.description: A cumulative reference that substantially reiterates verbatim the teachings of a reference previously relied upon or discussed may be considered repetitive and, for reexamination, could be excluded from consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such repetitive references are expected to be rare because most references add information or present it differently even when addressing the same subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices and wording when terminating or withdrawing because of Portola Packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution of an ongoing reexamination is terminated in compliance with Portola Packaging, or when a rejection is withdrawn to comply with Portola Packaging, specific notice language should be used in the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate or the Office action withdrawing the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of required wording are provided in the MPEP (references to In re Portola Packaging language and statement that no patentability determination has been made in the reexamination proceeding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming foreign priority or domestic benefit during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may correct failure to adequately claim foreign priority or domestic benefit during reexamination; renewal of previously made claims for foreign priority or domestic benefit is not necessary during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a priority claim was made before the patent was granted, submitting the certified copy in the reexamination proceeding is sufficient to perfect priority. If a petition to accept a delayed certified copy under 37 CFR 1.53(f)(3) is required, a grantable petition, appropriate fee, and attachments must be filed in the file of the application that matured into the patent; a letter must also be filed in the reexamination file notifying the Office that the petition is being concurrently filed in the application file. See MPEP § 215.02 and following subsections for additional procedural details.
